clue.text: Bread, spinach and turnip, a turnip's first eaten

indicators.note: eaten says the a plus initial letter go inside the spun and turned pieces, as food goes into a mouth
the word spinach is split as spin and ach, and to spin the letters ach is to whirl them into a new order
turnip splits as turn and ip, and to turn the letters ip is to flip them round
first, after turnip's, keeps only the opening letter of that vegetable

explanation.surface: A recipe list: a flatbread served with spinach and turnip, the turnip's first portion having been eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Both vegetables are split inside their own words: 'spin' works on 'ach' to make CHA, and 'turn' works on 'ip' to make PI. 'eaten' then puts A and T (turnip's first letter) inside CHA+PI.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened Indian flatbread, cooked on a griddle, so it is a kind of bread.

clue.text: Function where figure hosts number (not 10)

indicators.note: hosts means the figure holds the shortened number inside it, like a host with a guest

parts.note: a cone is a solid geometric figure

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the Roman ten from the number

parts.note: six is a number
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A maths student's note on a function in which one figure contains a number, minus ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not 10' uses the Roman numeral X for ten; 'hosts' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosine is one of the trigonometric functions, giving the ratio of adjacent side to hypotenuse.

clue.text: One carrying great weight now

indicators.note: carrying means the one holds the weight inside itself, as a porter carries a load

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards, or a single point
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pick up a heavy load immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately, without delay, which is what now means as a command.

clue.text: In autumn, group starts feeding together

indicators.note: feeding means those two initial letters go into the phrase for together, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: someone all there is mentally together, fully alert and sane

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of autumn and of group

explanation.surface: Come autumn, a flock begins feeding together.
explanation.walkthrough: The one-word definition 'In' is well hidden at the front, as in 'the in thing'. A and G, the first letters of 'autumn' and 'group', go inside ALL THERE, giving ALL THER(AG)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in is fashionable at the moment, just as the phrase describes a current craze.

clue.text: Old person beginning to regret satnav so?

parts.note: an Inca was one of the ancient people of Peru

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the opening letter of regret

explanation.surface: An elderly driver quickly regrets relying on a satnav.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question: a satnav is one example of an in-car device, hence the '?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A satnav is typically mounted on the dashboard, a gadget fitted inside a vehicle.

clue.text: Sweet thing, as French produce private parts

indicators.note: parts means the cheese is split open so the other piece can sit in the gap

parts.note: Brie is a soft cheese produced in France
one's own is private, belonging to oneself alone

explanation.surface: A suggestive line comparing a sweet treat to French goods that reveal intimate body parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private parts' looks like a single phrase, but 'private' gives OWN and 'parts' says BRIE opens to take it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a small square of rich chocolate cake, a sweet treat.

clue.text: Cried, describing Moby Dick?

definitions.meaning: to have wept noisily and childishly
playfully, covered in whale fat, as the great white whale of the novel would be

explanation.surface: Someone sobbed when describing the famous whale.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means wept noisily; the joke reading is an invented adjective, coated in the fat that whales have.

clue.text: Social occasion with some characters rolling over in ecstasy, groping

indicators.note: rolling over says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wild party scene, people rolling about in ecstasy and groping each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a wild party with some characters is a stretch, but the surface makes the meaning clear.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild party of unrestrained indulgence, a social gathering at its most riotous.

clue.text: Cooker cutting out? That's always happening!

indicators.note: cutting means the cooker slices into the middle of the phrase for out

parts.note: someone out is not in
an Aga is a British brand of heavy range cooker

explanation.surface: An exasperated cook groans as the oven cuts out yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a large cast-iron range cooker found in many British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone says in weary frustration when a familiar mishap repeats itself.

clue.text: Stimulate singer to perform in centre of Queens

indicators.note: in places the rearranged singer inside the middle letters
centre of keeps the middle two letters of Queens
to perform suggests the letters of singer acting out a new routine, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A promoter wants to pep up a singer to perform in the middle of Queens, New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queens' looks like the New York borough, but only its centre letters are used; 'to perform' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to fill with vigour, so it is a synonym for stimulate.

clue.text: Cylinder turns around

indicators.note: around says the word for turns is brought round to run the other way

parts.note: loops are turns, as in loops of a rope

explanation.surface: A cylinder rotates on its axis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses LOOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is a cylinder on which thread, film or tape is wound.

clue.text: Heading for carrots, one fetching for us cut vegetable

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter, the head, of carrots

parts.note: for us, something is ours, so us gives the possessive our

indicators.note: cut means the word for one fetching loses its last letter

parts.note: a getter is one who fetches or gets things

explanation.surface: A kitchen errand: someone fetching carrots for us also chops a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the final R from GETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A courgette, called zucchini in America, is a small green marrow eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Take the blasted thing from the pen of author

parts.note: to nick is to steal or take
a horn is a thing that is blasted, sounded by blowing
a work from the pen of a writer is by that writer

explanation.surface: An angry instruction to grab the wretched thing out of a writer's pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasted' looks like a curse but means blown, like a horn. Nick Hornby is the English novelist of High Fidelity and Fever Pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Hornby is a British writer of novels and memoirs, so he is an author.

clue.text: Midnight on a journey, excited

indicators.note: on means the middle of night comes after the earlier pieces in this across clue

parts.note: a go is a turn or trip, as in going on a journey
the middle letter of the word night is G

explanation.surface: Someone setting off on a trip at midnight, thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is read as the mid of 'night', the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, full of excitement and anticipation.

clue.text: Let out houses in game one's played

indicators.note: houses means the rearranged letters surround the other pieces, giving them a home
out signals the letters of let are put out of order

parts.note: whist is a card game

explanation.surface: A landlord letting out houses as part of some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' looks like renting, but 'out' is an anagram signal on 'Let' alone, making TLE; 'houses' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin whistle is a simple metal pipe, a musical instrument that is played.

clue.text: With flyer penned, doctor ratifies orders

indicators.note: penned means the bird is shut inside the rearranged letters, as in a pen
to doctor letters is to tamper with them, so ratifies is rearranged

parts.note: a tern is a seabird, a flyer

explanation.surface: A bird shut away while a physician signs off on official decrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the physician but is the anagram signal; 'penned' puts the bird inside the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Orders in the sense of brotherhoods or religious societies, groups bound by common membership.

clue.text: People in diagram may be found

indicators.note: in puts the people inside the chart

parts.note: a table is a chart or diagram of data
a race is a people, a group of common descent

explanation.surface: Individuals in a chart can be located.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that may be found can be tracked down, the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Book is easy there, but …

parts.note: a journey may be easy going there, but hard coming back

explanation.surface: Someone says booking is easy at the destination, then trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots complete the phrase: easy going there, but hard coming back. 'Book' names the answer as a type of book with stiff covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A book bound with rigid boards rather than paper covers is so named.

clue.text: Oodl — or poodle?

parts.note: the letters oodl are the body of poodle, a dog, with its outer letters stripped

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: is this word oodl, or should it be poodle?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the answer means the body, the inner letters, of a dog's name: pOODLe without its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle is a servile lackey, someone who does the menial work for a boss, as does a drudge.

clue.text: 11's distance to one Irish county and another?

parts.note: a long way is a great distance, and Longford is one Irish county, so this suggests a long way off
Down is another Irish county, in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A question about how far it is from one Irish county to another.
explanation.walkthrough: '11's' points to the answer to 11 Across: a novel by Nick Hornby. Down is a county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Nick Hornby's 2005 novel about four people who meet on a rooftop.

clue.text: Spread out on this beachhead, absolute beauty

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of beach is B
utter means absolute, as in utter nonsense
a dish is an attractive person, a beauty

explanation.surface: A sunbather lies spread out on the beach, looking utterly gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beachhead' looks like a military landing, but it is the head of 'beach'. 'Spread' is the noun, the dairy spread put out on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A butter dish is the plate or covered container on which butter is set out at table.

clue.text: Trade in communist merchandise ultimately gets me promoted

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of merchandise
promoted means raised up, and in a down clue the letters of me rise to read upwards

explanation.surface: A trader of communist goods finally sees themselves raised in rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem is to exchange something, such as a voucher or coupon, for goods: to cash it in.

clue.text: See 19
Spinner, figure surprisingly on the money

indicators.note: on means the rearranged letters follow after the money in this across clue

parts.note: a cent is a small unit of money

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of figure turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A spin doctor's figure is surprisingly accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' is the anagram signal on 'figure'; 'on' places the shuffled letters after the money in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrifuge is a machine that spins samples at high speed to separate their components.

clue.text: Meeting judge, shut case

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it in court

indicators.note: case takes the outer letters of shut, its casing

explanation.surface: A meeting with a judge, and the case is closed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret meeting between lovers, an arranged rendezvous.

clue.text: German rising and falling?

definitions.note: A German first name, spelt the same forwards and backwards

indicators.note: the name reads the same whether read up or down the grid, rising or falling

parts.note: A German first name, spelt the same forwards and backwards

explanation.surface: A German whose fortunes go up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German male first name, so a German man may bear it.

clue.text: 11's sin is so in Saladin?

wordplay.reading: S + A LAD + IN: SIN placed around A LAD

parts.note: in the name Saladin the letters S and IN sit around A LAD, a boy

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether the sultan Saladin was sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: '11's' points to the answer to 11 Across, a novel by Nick Hornby. Saladin splits as S + A LAD + IN, so SIN is around A LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Nick Hornby's 1998 novel about a London bachelor and a twelve-year-old boy.

clue.text: It's recalled, story without a name

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters of it are taken back to front

parts.note: the word it, with 's as a link

indicators.note: without means the letter a is dropped from the story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a story but cannot recall the author's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns IT into TI; 'without a' takes A from TALE to leave TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book or other work, or a designation like Lord or Dr.

clue.text: Opening clue perfect for discussion

parts.note: a key is a clue, as in the key to a puzzle

indicators.note: for discussion means as spoken, so the word for perfect is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: whole means complete or perfect

explanation.surface: A detective says the opening clue is ideal for talking about.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyhole is the opening in a lock into which a key is put.

clue.text: The oxygen group's proposition

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
R.E.M. is an American rock group, with 's as a link

explanation.surface: A chemistry claim: the oxygen group's proposed idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a statement proved, or to be proved, by reasoning: a mathematical proposition.
